text: (1) Fructosamine and glycated albumin (GA) may complement plasma glucose and HbA1c in diabetes diagnosis and monitoring, which are biased by clinical and analytical factors — notably in patients with rapid glycemic changes, red blood cell disorders, or renal disease. Across clinical settings, GA's diagnostic efficiency and standardization exceed fructosamine's, with less sensitivity to preanalytical variables, lower reagent cost, and automation on conventional instruments; further studies must confirm whether GA can replace HbA1c. (2) WFS1, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress regulator, is essential for glucose- and GLP-1-stimulated cAMP production and insulin biosynthesis/secretion. Glucose triggers WFS1 translocation from the ER to the plasma membrane, forming a complex with adenylyl cyclase 8 (AC8). ER stress and mutant WFS1 block this complex, reducing cAMP synthesis and insulin secretion, contributing to β-cell dysfunction and type 2 diabetes progression.
